question: If a genuinely incomplete wake greeting times out and the matching WS epoch is forcibly retired, does ordinary disconnect handling endanger background offline replay?
verdict: No source path found that deletes a ready archive merely due to cancellation or a chunk ACK. Use the existing disconnect ownership sequence. Interruption and retry costs remain; server durability/idempotency require formal-cloud verification.
coexistence: Normal wake waiting can overlap a previously started formal replay. main:12839-12846 does not exclude wake greeting, and audio_uplink.c:1024-1035 allows background traffic when no real-time sender is active or queued.
safety_chain: main:35072-35089 cancels the formal worker for its connection epoch before ws owner reuse. It waits up to 6000 ms; failure uses controlled restart rather than reusing an object still referenced by a worker.
offline_audio_spool.c:4370-4386 sets cancellation and wakes ACK waits. An in-progress send remains subject to its transport timeout.
replay_wait_ack checks cancellation before waiting, during each wait iteration, and after the event wakes (3056-3059,3075-3077,3085-3088). Setting the wake bits alone is not a successful ACK.

The same function rejects disconnected/wrong-epoch transport at 3070-3072 and checks the actual ACK ok, epoch, request and control/chunk kind at 3102-3109. ACK parsing also matches expected message type and, if present, segment at 4772-4781.

replay_one_ready waits specifically for offline_audio_commit_ack (3833-3840). remove(path) is only reached with err==ESP_OK, after that wait, and after the storage-busy check (3853-3863). A chunk ACK never enters this deletion branch.
Cancelled/disconnected/timeout replay keeps the file; replay_ready_impl only quarantines independently revalidated size/CRC corruption (4186-4202), not cancellation.
If the server committed but its ACK was lost or cancellation won, the local ready file stays. The next connection begins from the server's acknowledged offset and requires idempotent commit handling.

If a valid matching commit ACK was already accepted before cancellation, local deletion can still finish. That is safe only under the documented server contract that commit ACK means durable accepted storage; firmware cannot prove the server fsync/database semantics.
costs_and_constraints: The exceptional reconnect interrupts replay, may repeat data/control transactions and increases completion time. It is not zero-impact.
Cancellation exceeding the existing six-second owner fence can cause controlled reboot; persisted ready archives survive but unrelated volatile session state is lost.

Retire only the timed-out greeting's current epoch under a narrow reason, after checking it is still the unresolved transaction. Do not make ordinary healthy-connection playback errors force reconnect.
Do not change binding scope, reassign archives or bypass commit ACK checks as part of this fix. R3 owner isolation is a separate missing protection.

Existing replay buffers contain copies read from the archived file. Cancelling them does not delete the source. Recording staging/close workers are separate owners and must retain their existing gates.
targeted_verification: Force the genuine wake timeout while replay waits for begin ACK, while a chunk is being sent, while waiting for chunk ACK and while waiting for commit ACK.
Race cancellation with a correct commit ACK and with stale/wrong-epoch/wrong-request ACKs. Inspect ready-file retention/deletion and the cloud's unique committed segment count.
Drop commit ACK after server durability, reconnect and repeat begin/commit; verify no double-appended audio and eventual local deletion only after the new valid ACK.

Use an intentionally slow transport/SD read to exercise six-second cancellation fallback and boot recovery, without interpreting a retained local file as upload failure or a retry as duplicate user audio.
evidence_level: Read-only current-source control-flow review; no cloud action or product hardware test executed for this cross-check.
